label: M2.4-R0 temporal action abstraction feasibility: preregistration (research only)
question: does the 50 Hz per-tick decision create unnecessary temporal credit-assignment difficulty, and what action-persistence timescale does the existing behaviour justify?

policies.A: accepted N4B1C (FixedEscapePolicy, continuous Action; categorised by the teacher mapping)

tolerances.reference: mapped N4B1C teacher at 50 Hz (period 1) on the same R0 development episodes (paired seeds)

closed_loop.T2_escape_latency: median escape latency after the click <= reference + 0.04 s
closed_loop.T4_unnecessary: |unnecessary escapes / min - reference| <= max(1.0, 0.2 x reference)
closed_loop.T6_wall_speed: wall-contact fraction <= reference + 0.01 and max-speed fraction <= reference + 0.01
closed_loop.T7_no_new_pathology: no M2.1 anti-cheat flag absent from the reference (anti-cheat reference = the accepted N4B1C on the same episodes); turn-active fraction within +/- 20 % of the reference

open_loop.O1_escape_event_recall: fraction of teacher escape events reproduced (same side / strength) by the held stream within the decision interval that contains them >= 0.95
open_loop.O2_escape_delay: mean delay of reproduced escapes <= 0.04 s
open_loop.O3_turn_agreement: fraction of teacher TURN ticks where the held stream shows the same turn >= 0.80

tolerances.selection: the COARSEST cadence for which one variant passes every T and O criterion is recommended (outcome B). If none coarser than 20 ms passes: outcome C if the natural maneuver durations cluster into a small set, otherwise outcome A (keep 50 Hz). Benchmark score is not a selection criterion.
tolerances.observation_constraint: the unchanged observation carries the current frame + 4 history frames (5 ticks = 100 ms); a cadence coarser than 5 ticks leaves ticks that no decision observation contains. This is reported, not used to relax any tolerance.

dev_episodes.rule: TRAIN range [25e6, 30e6) minus M2.1 dev and M2.2/M2.3 TRAIN-VAL seeds; numpy default_rng(2400 + group); 16 per threat group, 12 per background family

credit_rollouts.rule: 21 units x (1 background + 6 threat), default_rng(2450), same pool, disjoint from the dev episodes; M2.3 candidate + its frozen seed-4 iteration-60 critic

windows.contexts: exclusive precedence: threat_window > perched (TOUCHDOWN / PERCHED) > lifecycle transition > wall (contact or near-wall) > threat_other > background_flight

eval_v3_design.name: M2-EVAL-v3
eval_v3_design.status: DEFINED ONLY in M2.4-R0; not generated, not run, never inspected during M2.4 hyperparameter selection
eval_v3_design.philosophy: unchanged M2.1 benchmark v2: exposure-controlled threat trials (4 families x 3 attacker levels, frozen attacker distributions, benchmark_definition sha256 127de798...) + background episodes (4 families); same metrics, constraints, anti-cheat flags, reward v2
eval_v3_design.seeds: threat group g (0..11, M2.1 order): 3_900_000 + 1000 x g + k, k = 1..40; background group g (12..15): 3_900_000 + 1000 x g + k, k = 1..20 (inside the registered EVAL range (3e6, 4e6); disjoint from EVAL v1 3.1e6-3.7e6 and v2 3_800_001-3_815_020, including their brain-noise seeds seed + 977)
eval_v3_design.size: 480 threat trials + 80 background episodes per policy (2 x the v2 threat count, for a paired 95 % CI of about +/- 0.045 instead of +/- 0.065 at the M2.3 effect size); the size increase is part of this preregistration
eval_v3_design.baselines: accepted N4B1C, no_escape, fixed_maneuver, random_legal and the three probes run once on v3 when it is frozen, before any M2.4 candidate exists
eval_v3_design.freeze_rule: seed manifest + sha256 of the definition committed and pushed BEFORE M2.4 full training; the M2.4 candidate is frozen (hash committed) before its single v3 run
eval_v3_design.m2_1_eval_status: M2.1 v2 EVAL observed by M2.2 and M2.3: valid historical evidence, not a future holdout
